A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDFilter and RED research. All supplied pages, equations, tables, and figures are readable. v1 ends after its references; v2 includes supplementary Sections 6–8. Newly included supplementary material can therefore be distinguished from material relocated from v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original denoising, super-resolution, tracking, ablation, runtime, SLAM, and video-reconstruction results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and additionally reports E-MLB denoising scores, calibration measurements, and component-level runtime results.

M1.justification: The three-stage filter is retained. v2 defines spatial normalization K by the number of directions with nonzero neighboring EDF, replacing the equality-based count in v1 Equations 32–33. Temporal optimization is less clear: v2's main text describes independently optimized height and bandwidth, while supplementary Section 7.4 retains the original alpha-h constraint. An implemented temporal redesign is therefore not established.

E1.justification: Ref-E evaluation and its qualitative example are removed. v2 directly evaluates E-MLB denoising across day/night and four noise levels; E-MLB already supported super-resolution and reconstruction experiments in v1. RED tasks and downstream applications remain, including super-resolution relocated to supplementary Section 8.6. Newly named SLAM datasets accompany existing sequences, not demonstrated new coverage.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain their comparator sets: Raw, EventZoom, EvFlow, MLPF, and Ynoise for filtering/tracking; EventZoom for super-resolution; and the same runtime and downstream baselines. The new E-MLB comparison reuses the existing filtering comparator set. Newly cited EBF and EDformer are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Tracking changes as specified from time-weighted L1 ITE in v1 Equation 56 to projected L2 ATE in v2 Equation 22, despite identical scores; this does not establish rerunning. v2 adds EDF-based ESR evaluation and revises RED's reported sequence count from 60 to 120 without changing the stated cameras or capture conditions. Scale-optimized NMSE remains in supplementary Equation 95 despite its omission from main-text Equation 21.

E4.justification: The temporal-model, spatial-norm, and sampling ablations are retained, with Compound sampling renamed Hybrid. New Section 8.7 and Table 6 separate prediction, update, and sampling costs and explain dependence on LUT-key count and output events. Supplementary calibration analyses also quantify acquisition accuracy.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports uncertainty for the existing acquisition system: 122727.4 ± 0.1 encoder counts per revolution, synchronization deviations of 10 ± 2 microseconds and 60 ± 10 microseconds, and approximately 0.1-pixel spatial deviation. Existing benchmark standard-deviation columns remain unchanged. Neither PDF specifies repeated-run counts or random seeds.

E6.justification: v2 adds E-MLB ESR results and calibration/component-runtime measurements, while removing Ref-E RMSE results, where EDFilter scored 0.092 versus EventZoom's 0.087. The new ESR table includes an exception to EDFilter's lead: ND16 night gives 1.00 versus EventZoom's 1.01. Matched RED denoising, super-resolution, tracking, overall runtime, SLAM, and reconstruction numbers are unchanged; no same-setting performance improvement is established.

T1.justification: Supplementary Sections 6–7 add substantial derivations and proofs absent from the supplied v1, including SDE-to-Fokker–Planck derivation, explicit spectral assumptions, likelihood/MLE derivations, and spatial uniqueness/sparsity proofs. Several underlying propositions and the multidimensional formulation already appeared in v1. The scalar reformulation also introduces a discrepancy: v2 Equation 4 omits the density multiplier on the drift term present in v1's flux formulation.

C1.justification: The central probability-flux filtering, O(1) processing, RED, and effectiveness claims remain. A limited substantive correction changes RED's contribution-list resolution claim from nanoseconds in v1 to microseconds in v2. Abstract and conclusion emphasis shifts toward denoising and motion fidelity, but super-resolution capability and downstream benefits remain claimed elsewhere.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1's interpretation of EVK4 noise through pixel size, texture complexity, and readout bandwidth. It adds explanations of gearbox backlash, camera-dependent synchronization error, and scan duration motivating 1-ms evaluation bins. The irradiance-versus-motion tradeoff and super-resolution spatial-diffusion limitation are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds sequential pseudocode and substantial RED reproduction details: encoder/gearbox configuration, calibration procedures, a 100-MHz logic analyzer, spatial alignment and cropping, and back-projected ground-truth generation. Baseline hyperparameters largely move intact to Section 8.5. Some information is lost, including v1's selected 10-/20-second evaluation durations and explicit ESVO/E2VID implementation links.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused from filtering, generation models, and evaluation datasets to discriminative/generative filtering and an explicit closest-prior comparison with DVS-Voltmeter. v2 positions its inference direction against that simulator. It adds EBF and EDformer while removing substantial coverage of other modeling, super-resolution, and evaluation work; this exceeds citation renumbering or bibliographic editing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed. Long derivations, implementation material, and super-resolution move into a separately organized supplement. The title changes from Event Signal Filtering to Event Stream Filtering, alongside terminology changes such as blob-to-point tracking.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are substantially redesigned, and apparatus and pattern illustrations are merged. Downstream tables are combined with reduced qualitative displays in Figures 8–9. v2 adds an ESR table and calibration illustrations, replaces/removes filtering examples, and relocates super-resolution displays to the supplement. Typography, captions, table styling, and page composition also change extensively.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through detailed calibration procedures and pseudocode, adds denoising evidence, and clarifies much of the presentation. However, conflicting main-text/supplement optimization and NMSE definitions, a changed tracking norm paired with identical scores, and the missing density factor in Equation 4 introduce reliability concerns. These benefits and unresolved inconsistencies prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
